newsitem.title: UK: Cash Brent broadly steady, CFDs talked firmer.
newsitem.headline: Cash Brent broadly steady, CFDs talked firmer.

text.p: Cash Brent crude was broadly steady in early talk on Thursday but CFDs showed signs of edging higher amid talk that U.S. refiner Koch was still looking for another early June cargo, traders said.
Koch has fixed the Hellespont Paramount to load 365,000 tonnes of Brent at Sullom Voe around June 6, picked up a June 5-7 cargo late on Wednesday at July Brent -10 cents.

July Brent was broadly steady at around $20.15 a barrel, in line with late U.S. dealing, and intermonth spreads were also holding onto Thursday's gains, June/July offered at +8 cents after trading at +7 cents.
July/August and August/September were little changed at -1/+2 cents and -1/+1 cent respectively in early talk, dealers said.
Brent CFDs for next week (May 27-30) were talked a couple of cents firmer at July -10/-8 cents with the following week also picking up three or four cents to -13/-10 cents.
"There's talk that Koch is probably still there to buy another Brent," said a trader.
Only one Brent cargo was scheduled to be nominated loading dates of June 6-8 on Thursday. Both June 5-7 Brents were kept on Wednesday.
Other North Sea crudes were also steady, with offshore loaders continuing to benefit from their fixed-freight advantage. North Sea tankers rates remain high despite easing slightly this week.
A late May loading cargo of Statjord fetched Dated Brent +31 cents on Thursday, traders said.
A slight improvement in European refining margins this week, albeit from very depressed levels, was also providing some support to wet market differentials, they said.
